title: Import Gmsh .msh 4.1 meshes
body:
**Background:** Many open meshing workflows produce Gmsh `.msh` files. Reading MSH 4.1 lets people bring an existing volume mesh into FieldCraft and set up, solve or export it, without any CAD geometry.

![An all-hex mesh in FieldCraft; an imported mesh shows up the same way](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/main/docs/media/bracket-hex.png)

## Current behaviour

FieldCraft cannot read a mesh without geometry. The only importers are `geometry.open` (SolidCraft designs) and `geometry.import.mesh` (face-tagged 3MF surfaces). "Orphan Mesh" is a greyed "coming soon (M6)" toolbar entry. A `.msh` file given to the surface importer is rejected as a broken 3MF package.

## Reproduction

On `main` at bf42d18 (2026-10-14), with a hand-written one-tetrahedron MSH 4.1 file:

```sh
cat > tet.msh <<'EOF'
$MeshFormat
4.1 0 8
$EndMeshFormat
$Nodes
1 4 1 4
3 1 0 4
1
2
3
4
0 0 0
1 0 0
0 1 0
0 0 1
$EndNodes
$Elements
1 1 1 1
3 1 4 1
1 1 2 3 4
$EndElements
EOF
echo '[{"command":"geometry.import.mesh","params":{"path":"tet.msh"}}]' > msh.json
cargo run -p fieldcraft-cli -- run msh.json
cargo run -p fieldcraft-cli -- commands | grep -i -e msh -e gmsh -e orphan
```

## Evidence

```
error: step 1 (geometry.import.mesh): invalid input: 3MF: not a zip package: invalid Zip archive: Could not find EOCD
```

No command mentions `msh`, `gmsh` or `orphan`.

## Expected behaviour

`mesh.import.orphan {"path": "part.msh"}` reads an ASCII MSH 4.1 file and replaces the mesh:
- nodes and elements keep their Gmsh tags as labels;
- every physical group becomes a set, named by its `$PhysicalNames` name.

The reader follows the public *Gmsh Reference Manual*, section "MSH file format" (version 4.1), and its "Node ordering" figures. **Do not read Gmsh's source code: it is GPL.**

## Investigation

- **Element types.** These are the MSH element type numbers for the kinds FieldCraft has:

  | Gmsh type | Gmsh element | FieldCraft kind | node order |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 2-node line | `rod2` | same |
  | 8 | 3-node line | `rod3` | same (ends, then middle) |
  | 2 | 3-node triangle | `tri3` | same |
  | 9 | 6-node triangle | `tri6` | same (edges 0-1, 1-2, 2-0) |
  | 3 | 4-node quadrangle | `quad4` | same |
  | 16 | 8-node quadrangle | `quad8` | same |
  | 4 | 4-node tetrahedron | `tet4` | same |
  | 11 | 10-node tetrahedron | `tet10` | **differs**: Gmsh's nodes 8 and 9 are swapped (Gmsh 8 is edge 2-3 and 9 is edge 1-3; FieldCraft has 1-3 then 2-3) |
  | 6 | 6-node prism | `wedge6` | same (0-1-2 normal towards 3-4-5 in both) |
  | 5 | 8-node hexahedron | `hex8` | same |
  | 17 | 20-node hexahedron | `hex20` | **differs**: Gmsh orders the edges 0-1, 0-3, 0-4, 1-2, 1-5, 2-3, 2-6, 3-7, 4-5, 4-7, 5-6, 6-7; FieldCraft orders them 0-1, 1-2, 2-3, 3-0, 4-5, 5-6, 6-7, 7-4, 0-4, 1-5, 2-6, 3-7 |

  - With `fc[k] = gmsh[p[k]]`:
    - tet10: `p = [0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,9,8]`;
    - hex20: `p = [0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7, 8,11,13,9, 16,18,19,17, 10,12,14,15]`.
  - Derive these from the manual's figures yourself and prove them with the mid-side test below; don't take this table on trust.
  - Refuse every other type by name and number: 7 (pyramid), 10 and 12 (9- and 27-node quads and hexes), 13, 18 and 19 (higher-order prisms and pyramids), and anything higher order. Type 15 (1-node point) is allowed only inside a 0-dimensional physical group, and becomes a node set.
- **Lower-dimensional physical groups become face sets.** In a volume mesh, Gmsh writes boundary triangles and quads as separate elements so that physical surface groups can name them. FieldCraft must **not** import those as shell elements: an unintended shell layer would change the stiffness. When the mesh has 3D elements:
  - map each 2D element of a physical group to the volume element face with the same corner nodes, giving an `ElementFace { element, face }` in a set's `faces`;
  - map each 1D element to the matching `ElementEdge`;
  - map each 0D point to a node.
  - A 2D element that matches no volume face is reported, and the import is refused, unless `"unmatched": "shell"` asks to keep it as an element.
  - A mesh whose highest dimension is 2 imports its triangles and quads as elements (plane or shell models). The same rule applies one level down for edges.
- **Sets.** Physical groups are reached through `$Entities`: each entity lists its physical tags, and each element block names its entity.
  - The set name is the `$PhysicalNames` name, or `physical_<dim>_<tag>` when there is none.
  - Names must pass `fieldcraft_model::check_name` (a letter, then letters, digits, `_` or `-`, at most 64 characters). Others are refused with the offending name; don't silently rename.
- **Sections to skip or refuse:**
  - Skip unknown sections (the manual says readers should ignore them): `$NodeData`, `$ElementData`, `$Periodic`, `$GhostElements`, `$Parametrizations`, comments.
  - Refuse binary files (file-type `1`) with "binary MSH not supported yet".
  - Refuse versions other than 4.1 with the version found (e.g. 2.2).
  - Refuse partitioned meshes (`$PartitionedEntities`) as not supported yet.
  - Nodes with `parametric = 1` carry extra parametric coordinates after x y z. Read them and discard them; never misalign.
- Open question for the maintainer: should importing replace the current mesh (like the meshers) or add to it? Proposal: replace, as `mesh.tet.generate` does, and refuse while geometry-tagged sets would lose their members. The command output lists what was replaced.

## Where to look

- [`crates/model/src/mesh.rs#L15`](https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/blob/develop/crates/model/src/mesh.rs#L15): `ElementKind` node order. [`#L140`](https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/blob/develop/crates/model/src/mesh.rs#L140): `faces()` (face numbering used by `ElementFace`). [`#L255`](https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/blob/develop/crates/model/src/mesh.rs#L255): `set_node`. [`#L269`](https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/blob/develop/crates/model/src/mesh.rs#L269): `set_element`, the checked ways to build a mesh.
- [`crates/model/src/sets.rs#L36`](https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/blob/develop/crates/model/src/sets.rs#L36): `Set` (nodes, elements, faces, edges by label). [`#L105`](https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/blob/develop/crates/model/src/sets.rs#L105): `add_set`.
- [`crates/model/src/lib.rs#L72`](https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/blob/develop/crates/model/src/lib.rs#L72): `MAX_LABEL`, `MAX_NODES`, `MAX_ELEMENTS` caps.
- [`crates/decks/src/abaqus.rs#L714`](https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/blob/develop/crates/decks/src/abaqus.rs#L714): how a writer walks elements and sets. A reader mirrors this.
- [`crates/io/src/mesh.rs#L41`](https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/blob/develop/crates/io/src/mesh.rs#L41): the `.fieldcraft` binary mesh reader, a model of hostile-input reading (every count checked against the bytes present before allocating).
- [`crates/io/src/fs.rs#L122`](https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/blob/develop/crates/io/src/fs.rs#L122): `read_capped`.
- [`crates/engine/src/cmd/geometry.rs#L35`](https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/blob/develop/crates/engine/src/cmd/geometry.rs#L35): `geometry.import.mesh`, an import command to copy (`file_param` with `Access::Read`).
- [`crates/engine/src/catalogue.rs#L307`](https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/blob/develop/crates/engine/src/catalogue.rs#L307): the planned `mesh.import.orphan` entry. Its icon `assets/icons/mesh.import.orphan.svg` already exists.

## What to build

1. **Parser in `fieldcraft-io` (L5)**, new module `crates/io/src/gmsh.rs`: `pub fn read_msh(text: &str, limits) -> Result<Imported>`. It takes text in and gives nodes, elements and sets out, with no file system, so it builds for wasm.
   - Line-oriented, with whitespace-separated tokens.
   - Every count (`numEntityBlocks`, `numNodes`, `numElements`, `numElementsInBlock`, …) is checked against `MAX_NODES` and `MAX_ELEMENTS` *and* against the lines that remain, before anything is allocated.
   - Tags must be in `1..=MAX_LABEL`. Coordinates must be finite and within `MAX_COORD`. Duplicate tags and elements that cite missing nodes are refused, naming the line number.
2. **Command in `fieldcraft-engine` (L6):** `mesh.import.orphan` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/mesh.rs`, registered in `cmd::ALL`.
   - Params doc: `{"path": "part.msh", "unmatched": "refuse|shell"}`. Format is chosen by extension; `.msh` only for now.
   - It builds the mesh through `set_node`, `set_element` and `add_set`, so a file can never hold what commands would refuse.
   - Output: `{"nodes": n, "elements": {"tet10": n, …}, "sets": [{"name", "nodes", "elements", "faces", "edges"}], "skipped_sections": [...]}`.
3. **Catalogue:** turn [`soon("mesh.import.orphan", …)`](https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/blob/develop/crates/engine/src/catalogue.rs#L307) into `ready(...)` with the tip "Import a mesh without geometry (Gmsh MSH 4.1)". Regenerate `docs/features.md`. Update ROADMAP.md M6 ("orphan-mesh import").
4. **Refuse by name:** binary files, versions other than 4.1, unsupported element types (number and name), partitioned meshes, truncated sections (`$EndNodes` missing, fewer lines than counted), bad names, unmatched boundary elements.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ASCII MSH 4.1 files with every supported element type import, with labels equal to the Gmsh tags.
- [ ] tet10 and hex20 are reordered. A test proves, for straight-edged elements, that every FieldCraft mid-side node lies at the midpoint of the two corners `ElementKind::edges()` gives it.
- [ ] `mesh.quality` reports every imported 3D element valid (positive Jacobian) for a hand-written file with one element of each kind.
- [ ] Physical volumes become element sets. Physical surfaces in a volume mesh become face sets (`ElementFace`), physical curves become edge sets, physical points become node sets. No shell elements are created in a volume mesh unless `"unmatched": "shell"`.
- [ ] Everything listed under "Refuse by name" fails with a message naming it, and leaves the model unchanged.
- [ ] Hostile files never panic and are refused quickly with small `Session::limits`. Cover: truncated at every line, counts of 10¹⁸, negative counts, tags of 0 and 2³², NaN and 1e400 coordinates, 10 MB lines, an element citing a missing node, duplicate tags.
- [ ] Hostile params (`path` missing, a number, a folder, `/dev/zero`, 100 000 characters) are added to `hostile_params_never_panic` ([`crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L330`](https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/blob/develop/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L330)).
- [ ] The catalogue entry is ready, and `docs/features.md` and ROADMAP.md are updated.

## How to test

- **Write the test files by hand** (as in the reproduction above), from the manual's format description. Never use files produced by commercial tools; files written by Gmsh itself are fine to try locally but must not be committed. `.msh` is plain text and needs no ATTRIBUTION row.
- **Round trip:** build a model with `mesh.block` (hex20 and tet10) and write it to MSH 4.1 text in the test with a tiny local writer. Read it back and compare node coordinates, connectivity and sets.
- **Solve check:** import a cantilever as hex20 with a physical surface on each end, clamp one set, load the other, and compare the tip deflection with the [cantilever-hex20 oracle case](https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/tree/develop/tests/oracle/cantilever-hex20) value.
- **Hostile:** a property-style loop that truncates a valid file at every byte and asserts `Err`, never a panic.

## References

- C. Geuzaine, J.-F. Remacle, *Gmsh Reference Manual*, section "MSH file format" (version 4.1) and "Node ordering": https://gmsh.info/doc/texinfo/gmsh.html#MSH-file-format (documentation only; Gmsh's source is GPL and must not be read).
- C. Geuzaine, J.-F. Remacle, "Gmsh: a 3-D finite element mesh generator with built-in pre- and post-processing facilities", *IJNME* 79(11):1309–1331, 2009.

## Getting started

```sh
git clone https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft && cd fieldcraft
cargo run -p fieldcraft-cli -- commands
cargo test -p fieldcraft-io
cargo test -p fieldcraft-engine
cargo clippy -p fieldcraft-io -p fieldcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

Read AGENTS.md (never-crash rules: input-derived numbers are hostile) before writing code.

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/jyviko/fieldcraft/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md) and comment to claim this issue before starting. Clean-room rules apply: public specifications, papers and analytic results only — no GPL code, no commercial-product files or output.
